_why: Mutant ids declared BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING for interp1d, each with the measurement behind it. `vit_mutate.py --equivalences` reads the KEYS of this object, so the claim and its reason live in one file, and a declared mutant LEAVES THE DENOMINATOR -- every entry is a claim somebody has to be able to answer. FIVE are declared and they fall into THREE reasons, two of which are proved exhaustively rather than argued (evidence/interp1d/equivalence_probe.txt) and one of which is a COUNT over the corpus the harness actually generated (evidence/interp1d/errmsg_extremes_probe.txt). What was NOT declared is the larger number: the first scoring run left THIRTEEN survivors at 0.865, and eight of those are gone -- not declared -- because R10 was added to the corpus (two boundary comparisons, the branches the kernel is also blind to) and four restatements were removed from the translation, including a `while (n > 0 && s[n-1] == ' ')` scan whose loosening mutant read the byte BEFORE the buffer. A survivor is a question about the instrument until the instrument has been asked.
20f2a843: compare_op '<' -> '<=' at `if (x < xData_min) xData_min = x;`, the MINVAL reduction. PROVED, not argued, and the proof is not the obvious one: loosening the comparison makes the loop RE-ASSIGN on a tie, and a re-assignment DOES change the stored bits -- 1,666 of 69,905 swept tuples have different bits in xData_min or xData_max. The signed zero is why: `-0.0 <= 0.0` is true where `-0.0 < 0.0` is false. What makes the mutant equivalent is that this unit reads the reduction ONLY through `xq <= xData_min` and `xq >= xData_max`, and IEEE says `+0.0 == -0.0`. evidence/interp1d/equivalence_probe.cpp sweeps every ordered tuple of length 0..4 over a 16-value set containing both zeros, duplicates, both infinities, a NaN, DBL_MAX/MIN and their negatives, crossed with every xq in the same set: (tuple, xq) pairs whose CONSUMER differs = 0. That is exhaustive over the only structure a reduction has -- its answer depends on nothing but the multiset of values and their signs. NOT REMOVED: the loop is gfortran's own MINVAL shape, seeded with HUGE so that a zero-size array answers +HUGE; `*std::min_element` seeds with element 1 instead and disagrees under a NaN.
23097b47: compare_op '>' -> '>=' at `if (x > xData_max) xData_max = x;`. The MAXVAL half of 20f2a843, same probe, same run, same 0. Both spellings are swept together in evidence/interp1d/equivalence_probe.cpp because a tie in one reduction and a tie in the other can occur in the same tuple.
b61327db: compare_op '>' -> '>=' at `n > 0 ? static_cast<size_t>(n) : 0` in `errmsg_trim`. The two differ only at `n == 0`, where the tight form yields the literal `0` and the loose form yields `static_cast<size_t>(0)` -- the same length. EXHAUSTIVE over the whole type rather than over the corpus: evidence/interp1d/equivalence_probe.cpp sweeps all 4,294,967,296 values of a 32-bit int and reports 0 at which the resulting view length differs. This is the strongest of the five: it is equivalent on every input the C type admits, not merely on the ones this campaign generates.
55e42d36: const_tweak '0' -> '1' at the SAME line -- `n > 0 ? static_cast<size_t>(n) : 0` becomes `... : 1`, so an ErrMsg field arriving with a non-positive length would be read as one byte instead of none. UNREACHABLE HERE, and measured rather than reasoned: evidence/interp1d/errmsg_extremes_probe.cpp is the shipped translation with three counters and nothing else changed, run over all 497 harness cases -- `ErrVar->n_ErrMsg on entry, min .. max  1 .. 10`, `calls with n_ErrMsg <= 0: 0`. THIS IS A BLIND SPOT AND NOT AN EQUIVALENCE, and the difference is stated rather than blurred: the `0` branch is the view's own NOT-ALLOCATED convention (`VIT_CHAR_UNALLOCATED` is `-1` in vit_types.h) and the generator has no rung that puts a CHARACTER extent at its unallocated sentinel or at zero. Recorded in DECISIONS.md as a candidate corpus addition, with the reason it was not taken inside this unit: the character-length ladder is an EXISTING block, and a rung added there shifts the random draws of every unit already scored.
e34d5cc4: compare_op '>' -> '>=' at `if (static_cast<int>(s.size()) > ErrVar->n_ErrMsg_cap)` in `assign_errmsg`. The two forms differ on exactly one input, `s.size() == n_ErrMsg_cap`. MEASURED over the corpus: the same probe reports `n_ErrMsg_cap, min .. max  4097 .. 4106`, `largest message offered to assign_errmsg  42`, `calls with s.size() == cap: 0` in 474 assignments. The capacity is `LEN(ErrMsg) + 4096` in the differential harness (harness/emit.py ALLOC_HEADROOM) and the same 4096 in the integrated build (vit_errorvariables_view.f90), and this unit's longest message is 42 characters, so the guard is true in every configuration this campaign can build. SAME SITE, SAME REASON, SAME DECLARATION as ReadAvrSWAP's e82a5f90, ExtController's 11d2c9cc and UpdateZeroMQ's ac7a5b72 -- the fourth unit to reach the `CHARACTER(:), ALLOCATABLE` assignment idiom, and the reason has not changed. NOT REMOVED: the guard is what makes an over-long assignment a REFUSAL rather than a truncation, and a truncated error message is the one wrong answer a bit comparison cannot catch. This unit carries ONE such guard where the first draft carried two -- the RoutineName prefix used to have a hand-written `memmove` with a capacity test of its own, and folding it into `assign_errmsg` removed a second unkillable site rather than declaring it.
